title: Pearl millet domestication in the West African Sahel (Manning et al. 2011 dates)
summary: Pearl millet was domesticated from a wild West African grass in the Sahel. The earliest secure evidence comes from the Lower Tilemsi Valley in Mali, where domesticated spikelet chaff in pottery temper at Er Negf dates to roughly 2579-2369 cal BCE. The crop later spread east across Africa and to South Asia.

uncertainty.note: Anchored on the Er Negf pottery-temper AMS date of 2579-2369 cal BCE (3980 +/- 31 BP), reported from Manning et al. 2011. Manning et al. noted the temper may contain old carbon, so the true age could be younger; genetic work suggests a domestication date near 2800 BCE. 2500 BC is the round figure used in the literature.

where.modern_name: Lower Tilemsi Valley, Gao Region, Mali (pin at Tilemsi commune)
where.historical_name: No polity; Saharan-Sahelian pastoralist, fishing and cultivating communities of the Tilemsi Valley

importance.justification: Pearl millet became a staple of dry-land farming across Africa and South Asia; the Tilemsi evidence is the earliest secure record of its domestication.
